sense.evidence: Terms fit: "The mob on the other side", "on side with him", "a big hand in", "stayed put", "having a go at popular amusements", "ciggies".

register.evidence: Level 4 in voice, slang steady but restrained for an obituary ("mob", "on side", "ciggies", "having a go"). No swearing, within the dial. A touch light.

tone.evidence: Keeps the obituary's measured tone and its one dry note: "there's this odd one that crops up: \"Rhetoric Made Racy.\""

flow.evidence: Smooth: "His pen and his voice barely got a rest in the last fifty years."

variety.evidence: Varied enough: "mob", "on side", "a fair bit", "switched over", "stayed put", "having a go", "ciggies"; nothing leaned on.

B.summary: The most even rendering: faithful, natural and varied, keeping the obituary's measured tone.

meaning.evidence: Facts survive, but some swaps tilt them: "barracking for prohibition and that sort of carry-on" disparages the causes, "who was his offsider in heaps of his many goings-on" turns his partner into his sidekick, and "which he reckoned" softens a direct quote.

sense.evidence: "barracking for" fits (supporting a side); "offsider" strains for a wife who was a partner; "that sort of carry-on" and "goings-on" carry a dismissive sense the original lacks; "his gob" for his voice.

authenticity.evidence: Natural idiom ("a red-hot go", "of that ilk", "a real character", "never-say-die"), but piled on: "Among the reform mob, not many could've matched Dr. Crafts for sheer hard yakka. His pen and his gob barely got a breather".

register.evidence: Full level 4 and within vulgarity 1 ("a bloody mountain of stuff"), but the weight is heavy for an obituary and nudges past the brief.

tone.evidence: The obituary turns mocking in places: "that sort of carry-on", "He wrote a bloody mountain of stuff on moral questions.", "his gob".

flow.evidence: Readable, with some clunky joins: "Dr. Crafts, who the blokes fighting the laws he pushed reckoned was a \"reform fanatic,\" was a real character".

variety.evidence: Very varied: "barracking", "carry-on", "a red-hot go", "of that ilk", "offsider", "gob", "churning out", "never-say-die".

essence.evidence: Recognisably the obituary, but the dismissive asides change its character from a neutral record to a send-up.
